# Posterior contraction of Bayesian tree reconstruction without branch-length bounds

**Setting.** Data are $k$ independent sites, each an allele configuration $\mathbf{a}_j \in H^n$ at the $n$ leaves of a tree $(T, \mathbf{x})$, generated by a continuous-time Markov substitution model with rate matrix $\mathbf{Q}$ on a finite allele set $H$ and root distribution $r$; branch lengths are $\psi_T(\mathbf{x})$ for a parametrization $\mathbf{x} \in (0,\infty)^{m(T)}$. The parametrization is identifiable: $P_{\theta_0} = P_\theta \Rightarrow \theta_0 = \theta$. A posterior $\Pi^{(n)}(\cdot \mid \mathbf{a}_1, \dots, \mathbf{a}_k)$ *contracts at rate* $\varepsilon_k$ around $(T_0, \mathbf{x}_0)$ if it puts vanishing mass outside Hellinger balls of radius proportional to $\varepsilon_k$ around $P_{(T_0,\mathbf{x}_0)}$.

**General theorem.** Assume identifiability, and that either $n$ stays bounded or the data-generating trees are nested restrictions of one infinite-leaf tree. Let $L_f(T)$ be the set of branch-length vectors whose external branches all have length at least $f$ and $U_g(T)$ the set whose branches all have length at most $g$. If there are $\varepsilon_k, \zeta_k \to 0$ with $\zeta_k \le \varepsilon_k$, $k\zeta_k^2 \to \infty$, sieve levels $f_k \to 0$, $g_k \to \infty$, and $C > 0$ such that (i) the sieve $\{L_{f_k} \cap U_{g_k}\}$ has metric entropy at most $k\varepsilon_k^2$, (ii) its complement has prior mass at most $e^{-(C+4)k\zeta_k^2}$, and (iii) the prior puts mass at least $e^{-Ck\zeta_k^2}$ on a Euclidean neighbourhood of $\mathbf{x}_0$ of radius proportional to $\zeta_k^2$ within $T_0$, then the posterior contracts around $(T_0, \mathbf{x}_0)$ at rate $\varepsilon_k$.

**Corollary (Kingman coalescent prior).** Let $\Pi^{K,n}$ be the Kingman coalescent on ranked rooted ultrametric trees (holding times $X_i \sim \mathrm{Exp}\binom{i+1}{2}$), and let $(T_0, \mathbf{x}_0)$ be an infinite-leaf tree in the support of its projective limit, observed through nested restrictions with coupled Poisson mutation processes. If $n = n_k$ grows so slowly that $\log k \ge n^2/C^2$ for a constant $C$, the posteriors contract at rate

$$\varepsilon_k \asymp k^{-1/2}(\log k)^{3/4 + \beta/2} \quad\text{for every } \beta > 1.$$

**Corollary (uniform topology prior).** The same rate holds for the prior that is uniform on the $(2n-5)!!$ unrooted binary topologies with independent $\mathrm{Exp}(\lambda)$ lengths on all $2n-3$ branches, provided $\mathbf{Q}$ is $r$-reversible.

## Proof sketch

The general theorem instantiates the Ghosal–Ghosh–van der Vaart contraction theorem with sieves defined by lower bounds on external branch lengths and upper bounds on all branch lengths. The key estimate is that on $L_f(T)$ the likelihood of each site is bounded below by a constant of order $(\eta f)^{nw}$, where $w$ mutations suffice to reach any allele and $\eta$ is a minimal mutation rate; this makes Kullback–Leibler divergence Lipschitz in $\mathbf{x}$ and controls the entropy. Exponential holding times make the sieve-complement mass explicit (via $\mathbb{P}(X < f) \le \lambda f(1 + \lambda f/2)$ and a union bound), and Borel–Cantelli shows the infinite tree's shortest branches shrink only polynomially. No discretization or a priori boundedness of branch lengths is needed, which covers the priors used by BEAST, MrBayes and RevBayes; the price is that $k$ must grow super-exponentially in $n$.
